findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext values. EC2 user data is readable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host (or via SSRF) and is stored in Terraform state, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is present, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. On an internet-facing web server whose user data contains plaintext AWS keys, this makes SSRF-based metadata and credential theft trivial.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true routed to an internet gateway and attached to a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH and HTTP, giving it direct internet exposure while holding plaintext credentials in user data.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's root volume may be created without EBS encryption, leaving data at rest (including the cached credential-bearing user data) unencrypted.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet on an instance that receives a public IP, enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS/HTTPS listener is configured, so all web traffic to the host traverses the public internet in cleartext.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised host.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data on the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted.

The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is configured, so a persistent unencrypted copy of the data exists that can be restored or shared without key-based access control.

The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network flow records revealing internal topology and traffic patterns are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or restrictive bucket policy is defined, so an accidental public ACL or policy could expose the network telemetry stored in this bucket.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, permitting log data to be read or written over cleartext HTTP.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with a route table pointing 0.0.0.0/0 at the internet gateway, gives every instance in this subnet a public IP and direct internet reachability by default.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the internet-gateway route table cause all instances in this subnet to receive public IPs, removing the network boundary for workloads that should be private.
